# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 29 (Bu-Vb Pc29)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc29
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 29
**Title (English, from literature):** Eating food prepared on a nun’s instruction
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 29 (*Paripācita*) is a monastic rule in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka prohibiting monks from consuming almsfood whose preparation or donation has been prompted or instigated by a nun (*paripācita*) [Hüsken 1997]. A monk who knowingly consumes almsfood procured through such intervention commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [Hüsken 1997]. In her analysis of the Vinaya's gender regulations, Ute Hüsken contextualizes Pācittiya 29 within a series of rules (such as Nissaggiya Pācittiya 4, 5, and 17, as well as Pāṭidesanīya 1) designed to prevent monks from soliciting, accepting, or benefiting from material support and food brokered by nuns [Hüsken 1997].

 Text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus identifies extensive shared formulaic passages within the Pali Vinaya, most notably with Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga rules Pc 85, Pc 46, Pc 32, and Pāṭidesanīya 3 [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistically, DharmaNexus identifies textual alignments with Tibetan canonical Vinaya treatises and commentaries, including the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104), the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkā Vinayasamuccaya* (D4106), the *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* (D0007), and the *Vinayasūtravṛtti* (D4122), alongside Sanskrit parallels in Jayarakṣita's *Sphuṭārthā Śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkā* and the *Divyāvadāna* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying Vibhaṅga narrative has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
